newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan postpones visit by China business group.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan postpones visit by China business group.

text.p: A visit to Taiwan by a China business delegation has been postponed indefinitely amid Taipei's tightening of economic policy towards Beijing, an organiser of the trip said on Friday.

A private Taiwan foundation aimed at promoting cross-strait business links had planned to invite Guo Dongpo, chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, to head a business delegation to the island for a 10-day visit starting on Friday, the organiser from the foundation said.
"We are told to wait for official documents. The government has not informed us whether they will be allowed to visit or not," the organiser said.
"It did not explicitly reject our application, but it did not say why it hasn't approved the application," the organiser who declined to be identified, said by telephone.
Tsai Lien-sheng, executive-secretary of the economics ministry's Investment Commission, said the government was still reviewing the case, but declined to give further details.
Local media said it was part of the government's recent attempt to cool business ties with the mainland.

Taiwan, a rival of communist China since a civil war spilt them in 1949, has expressed concern its economy was becoming too dependent on China, which could make the island politically vulnerable to its arch rival.
More than 30,000 Taiwan firms have invested an estimated US$30 billion in China since an unofficial thaw in bilateral relations began in the late 1980s.
Taiwan has recently drafted a new set of criteria which would be used to gauge and regulate the level of local investment in rival China.
